turns.content: Three vicinal diols undergo acid-catalyzed pinacol rearrangement: 3-methyl-4-phenylhexane-3,4-diol; 3-(4-hydroxyphenyl)-2-phenylpentane-2,3-diol; and 1,1,2-tris(4-methoxyphenyl)-2-phenylethane-1,2-diol. What mechanistic decisions are needed to predict the major ketone from each substrate?
State a systematic procedure for choosing which hydroxyl is protonated and lost, which carbocation is favored, which group migrates, and which carbon becomes the carbonyl carbon.
Explain how carbocation stabilization and migratory aptitude interact in an acid-catalyzed pinacol rearrangement, especially for aryl-substituted substrates.
Apply that framework to 3-methyl-4-phenylhexane-3,4-diol and determine product A, naming the favored migration and ketone.
Apply the same analysis to 3-(4-hydroxyphenyl)-2-phenylpentane-2,3-diol and determine product B.
For the third substrate, compare 4-methoxyphenyl and phenyl migration under acidic conditions and explain the electronic preference.
Use that comparison to determine product C from 1,1,2-tris(4-methoxyphenyl)-2-phenylethane-1,2-diol.
List the major products A, B, and C and give the key stabilization or migratory-aptitude reason for each assignment.
Cross-check each structure by identifying the carbonyl-forming carbon and the group that migrates.
Report the final systematic product names for A, B, and C.
